headline.caveat: >$5B of Dell AI servers with NVIDIA GB200 racks for Colossus (initial reported order, Feb 2025); xAI subsequently shifted ~$6B of orders from Supermicro toward Dell, and follow-on orders have grown the relationship (Dell counts xAI among its named AI customers behind its $51.3B AI backlog).

realized_to_date.caveat: GB200 deliveries ran through 2025; cumulative payments not disclosed (xAI is private; Dell does not break out customers).

nature_md: Dell supplies NVIDIA GB200-based rack-scale AI servers to xAI for the Colossus buildout in Memphis — an initial ~$5B order reported Feb 2025, growing as xAI shifted ~$6B of orders away from then-troubled Supermicro (DOJ accounting probe) and split subsequent GB300-generation orders between Dell and Supermicro. Standard hardware purchase with delivery-based payment; xAI's extreme buildout tempo (racks energized within weeks of delivery) makes it one of Dell's marquee AI accounts alongside CoreWeave and IREN.

accounting.payer_treatment_md: xAI capitalizes servers as fixed assets (or routes them through its GPU-leasing SPV structures — see xai-gpu-spv entity — to keep debt off its own balance sheet), depreciating over 4-6 years; funded by equity/debt raises, not operating cash flow.
accounting.payee_treatment_md: Dell books ISG hardware revenue on delivery at thin AI-server margins (pass-through NVIDIA content dominates BOM); xAI orders sit within its $51.3B AI backlog and ~$60B FY27 AI revenue guide.
